answer: Every new agent must post a stake before its whisper of an opinion counts. Each identity is a vertex in the trust graph, where honest conduct slowly compounds into reputation. When peers detect a forged attestation, they act as a quill signing an indictment: the guilty stake is slashed and burned, paying the reporter directly. An attacker must lock fresh capital for every fake identity, forfeit it on the first misstep, and still wait epochs for influence to accrue. Sybil rings thus become capital traps whose expected cost exceeds any gain from fraudulent votes.
